geos.label: South Bay
geos.blurb: San Jose, Saratoga, Sunnyvale, Mountain View

meta.standfirst: Arts, music, and worthwhile oddities, ordered by remove from Mountain View.

peak.note: 17 stacks up at Los Gatos from mid-afternoon
weekend beach traffic northbound in the evening
101 south through Sunnyvale is stop-and-go from 4
101 north is the worst of the peninsula — 280 is usually faster
101 north clogs from Redwood City at 3:30; the 280 split at Daly City is the second squeeze
weekend midday backs up into the city
the Caldecott is the pinch — eastbound clears by 7
Waldo Grade northbound is the bottleneck

local arterials get slow around the school and commute peak

events.title: Bobby McFerrin
events.note: Ten Grammys and a voice used as a whole rhythm section — overtone singing, body percussion, improvised call-and-response with whoever is in the room. A 600-seat listening room is an absurd place to catch him. Start time not printed on the mirror; check before you go.

events.title: Built to Spill, PLAYDEAD
events.note: Doug Martsch's long guitar lines still unwind the way they did on Perfect From Now On — patient, slightly out of tune, building to something. Two nights here, Monday and Tuesday; the band also plays Santa Cruz on Wednesday.

events.title: Berkeley Mt Zion 80th Anniversary Celebration
events.note: An East Bay Black church marking eighty years by taking over a jazz club for the night. Gospel in a room built for close listening rather than a sanctuary — a different thing entirely from hearing it on a Sunday.

events.title: GLU
events.note: Bedroom-scale electronic pop with the seams left showing. A Monday booking at Brick & Mortar usually means a band on the way up rather than one passing through.

events.title: Death Guild
events.note: The longest-running goth night in the United States, six DJs across two rooms, still going every Monday. 18+. If you have never been, this is the standing fixture the rest of the country's goth nights were modelled on.

events.title: American Doctor, with filmmaker Poh Si Teng in person
events.note: Documentary on a physician's working life, with the director present for the Q&A. She is at the Roxie repeatedly this week — Monday, Tuesday, Friday and Saturday — which is unusual enough to be worth building an evening around.

events.title: Garden Bros Nuclear Circus
events.note: A touring circus pitched in a drive-in lot, two shows a day through Thursday. Listed for completeness rather than recommended — this operator's reviews are mixed and the programme was not verifiable beyond the aggregator.

events.title: David Byrne: Who Is the Sky Tour
events.note: The American Utopia staging turned Byrne's band into a marching, barefoot, wireless organism, and the current tour keeps that logic. Doors 6:30. The Greek is a stone bowl on a hillside — it gets cold after dark regardless of the afternoon.

events.title: Black Marble, Serfs
events.note: Chris Stewart's one-man cold-wave project — cheap drum machines, buried vocals, melodies that sound like they were recorded through a wall. Warmer live than on record. All ages.

events.title: Brainstory, BOLERO!, Radio Veloso
events.note: Rialto trio on Big Crown doing loose, unhurried soul with a jazz player's harmony underneath — closer to Shuggie Otis than to the retro-soul revival. The best-value bill of the night anywhere in the city.

events.title: Death Lens, Heart to Gold, Grave Secrets, Garage Spiders
events.note: Four bands for under thirty dollars, LA garage-punk at the top. Doors at seven, so this one actually ends at a reasonable hour.

events.title: Keiko Matsui
events.note: Contemporary-jazz pianist with a large international following and a lyrical, unhurried touch. Two nights, Tuesday and Wednesday.

events.title: HLLLYH, Dauber, Squishers
events.note: The Mae Shi's noisier descendant, in a 150-capacity Telegraph Avenue bar that books the shows nobody aggregates. Transit is the sane way to downtown Oakland after dark.

events.title: Molly Santana, NORTH WEST
events.note: Atlanta rapper working the woozy, half-sung end of trap. The Midway is a warehouse in Dogpatch with real parking, which is rare enough in this city to matter.

events.title: Noe Valley Night Market
events.note: Food and maker stalls in the town square on a Tuesday evening — small, local, and over by eight. The kind of thing that never reaches a ticketing platform.

events.title: Civic Center Soundtrack
events.note: Free lunchtime music and food trucks on the plaza between the library and City Hall. Runs Tuesdays; the lineup is announced late and was not published at compile time.

events.title: People in Plazas: Jazz Concert
events.note: A free hour of jazz in a downtown privately-owned public space — the programme that keeps those plazas legally public. Performer not named in the listing.

events.title: Sips & Sounds of Summer
events.note: Free Tuesday-evening music on the lawn near Left Bank, running through September. The series is confirmed for August Tuesdays; this week's act was not published, so treat the booking as unverified.

events.title: SF StorySLAM: Serendipity
events.note: Open-draw storytelling — names into a hat, five minutes each, no notes. Half the value is watching people fail gracefully in front of a room.

events.title: SF Politics 101: Wild History and How City Hall Works
events.note: SPUR explaining the machinery — supervisors, ballot measures, why nothing gets built. Free, and more entertaining than it sounds given the city's actual history.

events.title: Peter Relic with Jeff Chang: Bust a Move
events.note: Two serious hip-hop writers in conversation — Chang wrote Can't Stop Won't Stop, which is still the standard history. Free, and the Ferry Building store is small enough that arriving late means standing.

events.title: San Jose Giants vs. Visalia Rawhide
events.note: Single-A ball in a 4,200-seat park where you can hear the infield chatter. First of a four-game homestand against Visalia; eleven dollars gets you in.

events.title: OSEES ft. Brigid Dawson, Traps PS
events.note: John Dwyer's band running four consecutive nights in a 500-cap room, with Brigid Dawson back on the bill — her harmonies are the thing the later, heavier lineups lost. Wednesday through Saturday; Friday adds Gumby's Junk. Doors 7:30, all ages.

events.title: Courtney Barnett, Zoh Amba
events.note: Three nights at the Fillmore, and the support is the news: Zoh Amba is a free-jazz tenor player out of the Tennessee mountains, which is not a pairing anyone would have predicted. Barnett's deadpan and her guitar have both got heavier since Tell Me How You Really Feel.

events.title: Train, Barenaked Ladies, Matt Nathanson
events.note: A three-act nostalgia package that will fill the lawn cheaply. Bike the path from Mountain View rather than pay $40 to park; the Shoreline lot exit after a sold-out show is its own event.

events.title: Nonpoint, Spineshank, Drawing Heaven
events.note: Two survivors of the late-nineties nu-metal wave on a co-headline. Spineshank's industrial edge has aged better than most of that scene. Early doors.

events.title: The Hot Takes, The DisRespectors, Neon Ships
events.note: Thirteen dollars for three local bands on a Wednesday — the cheapest ticket in the digest this week. Bottom of the Hill has announced it closes at the end of 2026, so the arithmetic on nights like this is finite now.

events.title: Nox Novacula, The Discussion
events.note: Seattle darkwave in a 150-capacity Mission bar. Rooms this size are where the genre actually works — the reverb has nowhere to go.

events.title: Los Cenzontles
events.note: San Pablo's forty-year-old Mexican traditional-arts academy, playing son jarocho and norteño as living repertoire rather than heritage display. They have recorded with Los Lobos, David Hidalgo and Taj Mahal without ever leaving the East Bay.

events.title: Winter Animals, Apprehenchmen, We Are Leaves
events.note: Three Bay bands on a midweek bill at Telegraph's smallest working stage. No lineup information beyond the names — go for the room.

events.title: We Can Love It Together: Creativity Explored Short Film Fest
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Two decades of films and animation made by artists at Creativity Explored, the Mission studio for artists with developmental disabilities. Free — and Wednesday is YBCA's free gallery day, so GaHee Park's Behind the Curtain upstairs costs nothing either.

events.title: Free Art Workshop: Watercolor Flower Paintings
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: A collaborative still life in the Grand Lobby, materials provided. Free but registration is required, which is the only thing standing between you and a free afternoon.

events.title: CatVideoFest 2026
events.note: Seventy minutes of curated cat footage, with proceeds going to local animal welfare. Precisely as advertised, taken entirely seriously by the audience. Also Saturday at 4:55.

events.title: Almost Midnights: After Hours
events.note: Scorsese's one comedy, and the most anxious film ever made about trying to get home from SoHo. Part of the Roxie's late-night strand.

events.title: San Francisco Time Machine with Peter Hartlaub
events.note: The Chronicle's culture critic digging through the paper's own archive — photographs, ephemera and the city's forgotten embarrassments, presented live. Time not published; check before setting out.

events.title: The Faight Community Art Jam
events.note: Open studio night in the upstairs gallery room — bring your own project or use what is there. Free with RSVP; artist-run and unpolished in the way that makes these worth attending.

events.title: Son Rompe Pera, Inti Mystica
events.note: Three brothers from Naucalpan who inherited their father's marimba and pointed it at punk — cumbia sonidera played with distortion pedals and a garage band's tempo. One of the few acts that genuinely earns the word riotous. The best show in the city on a crowded Thursday.

events.title: Muse, Portugal. The Man, The Temper Trap
events.note: Maximalist stadium rock delivered without irony, plus a genuinely strong pair of openers. The largest booking within twenty minutes of the origin all week.

events.title: Annual Freight Fiddle Summit
events.note: The Freight's yearly gathering of fiddlers across traditions — Irish, old-time, Cajun, klezmer, whoever they have got — trading tunes on one stage. The lineup is announced late and was not posted at compile time.

events.title: Miko Marks residency, with Kiazi Malonga
events.note: Marks left Nashville when country would not have her and rebuilt a career out of Oakland; her records now do what the genre claims to. Kiazi Malonga is a Congolese master drummer, which makes this pairing the most interesting thing on the East Bay bill this week.

events.title: Ledisi
events.note: Oakland-raised, thirteen Grammy nominations deep, and a voice built for an outdoor room this size. The hillside gets cold once the sun drops behind the ridge — bring more than you think.

events.title: Nerf Herder, Pulsars, Dog Party
events.note: Santa Barbara nerd-punk lifers, best known for a theme tune they wrote in an afternoon. Two nights with different support — Sacramento's Dog Party on Thursday are the reason to take this one.

events.title: OTHA
events.note: Swedish pop with an unusually dry production ear — sparse, rhythmic, closer to Robyn's colder records than to the Scandinavian export sound.

events.title: Mamamoo: 2026 US Tour
events.note: The K-pop group that actually sings live, and has for a decade. An arena show, so listed for completeness rather than featured.

events.title: Hermanos Espinoza
events.note: Regional Mexican at the Civic — the strand of South Bay programming that fills a 3,000-seat hall and rarely appears in an English-language listings column.

events.title: Very Paranoia, Stepmother, Replica Watch
events.note: Local post-punk on a Thursday in a room that holds a hundred and fifty people. Descriptors here are inferred from the booking pattern, not from hearing the bands.

events.title: Sugar Candy Mountain, Sandy's
events.note: Oakland dream-pop in a hillside botanical garden at golden hour — one of the better-set concerts the East Bay puts on, and the setting does most of the work. It is a canyon; it gets cold early.

events.title: How to Become a Silicon Valley Creep (In 10 Easy Steps)
events.note: Adrian Daub (Stanford, and the author of What Tech Calls Thinking) with Moira Donegan, taking apart the valley's self-mythology in front of an audience that mostly works in it. 21+.

events.title: SOMA Nights Block Party and Night Market
events.note: Six blocks of Folsom closed for the fourth-Thursday street party — food, vendors, live music and more than twenty businesses running their own activations. August adds a plant swap and a petting zoo at Hallam. Free, and the best free thing midweek.

events.title: Movies on the Square: free double feature
events.note: Family film at six, main feature at half past eight, on the square outside the old courthouse. Twentieth year. Caltrain Redwood City is three minutes' walk, which beats hunting the garage.

events.title: Town of Colma Free Summer Concert Series
events.note: On the grass behind the community centre, August Thursdays. BART Colma genuinely beats driving from anywhere south. This week's band was not named in any listing found.

events.title: R.O.I. (Return on Investment)
events.note: New work on the Playhouse's second stage, running to 5 September. The company runs both its stages concurrently all summer, so there is theatre here on nights when the bigger houses are dark.

events.title: American Pachuco: The Legend of Luis Valdez
events.note: Portrait of the founder of El Teatro Campesino, who built Chicano theatre out of the Delano grape strike and then made Zoot Suit and La Bamba. Local history in the strongest sense.

events.title: San Jose Giants vs. Visalia Rawhide
events.note: Third game of the Visalia homestand. Weeknight crowds are thin enough to move seats after the second inning.

events.title: W.I.T.C.H.
events.note: We Intend To Cause Havoc — the Zambian band who invented Zamrock in the seventies, most of them presumed lost, reconstituted around surviving frontman Jagari Chanda and touring again. Fuzz-rock built on Zambian rhythm. The only thing in the outer region this week that justifies the drive over the hill, and it clears that bar easily.

events.title: Bill Callahan, Wendy Eisenberg
events.note: The former Smog, singing in that low unhurried baritone about dogs, rivers and marriage. Wendy Eisenberg's guitar playing goes somewhere else entirely. Sold out at the venue — resale only, and be sceptical of any listing offering it free.

events.title: 5 Seconds of Summer, The Band Camino
events.note: Second of three consecutive Shoreline nights. Expect the Amphitheatre Parkway approach to be solid from six; the bike path is not an exaggeration as advice.

events.title: The Greyboy Allstars
events.note: San Diego's boogaloo and deep-funk revivalists, playing a movie palace rather than a club. Karl Denson on saxophone is the engine. Doors 7.

events.title: Bob Schneider, Matt Jaffe
events.note: Austin songwriter with a twenty-year local monopoly on Monday nights at the Saxon Pub, playing a 500-seat Peninsula room. Matt Jaffe is Bay Area and sharper than the billing suggests. Doors 7; Caltrain Menlo Park is four minutes away.

events.title: Sweet Pill, Deux Visages, Stereosity
events.note: Philadelphia emo with a vocalist who can actually belt, which is rarer in the fifth wave than it should be. Time and price were not posted on the venue's page.

events.title: Nerf Herder, Ridel High, The Kegels
events.note: Second Nerf Herder night with a different undercard. If you are choosing, Thursday's bill is stronger; this one is for the Ridel High reunion.

events.title: My New Band Believe
events.note: No information available beyond the booking. Rickshaw's Friday nights lean indie and danceable; treat the descriptor as the room's habit rather than the band's.

events.title: Pokémon Rap Concert: Genwunner vs. Cam Steady
events.note: Two Pokémon rappers, timed precisely to the World Championships two miles away at Moscone. Filed under oddities without apology. 18+.

events.title: Öona Dahl & David Hohme
events.note: Deep, hypnotic, slightly psychedelic house across a long set. Public Works runs two rooms; Casa Tulum is on the other one the same night if you want something brighter.

events.title: Feed Me
events.note: Jon Gooch's long-running electro-house alias, all serrated basslines and cartoon menace. A big warehouse room suits it.

events.title: Martyr Princess, DJ Goth Spice, Gremlita, LOBOTTOMY
events.note: Live acts and DJs sharing a Friday bill — the sort of mixed-format night small rooms do well and larger ones cannot book. Take BART.

events.title: Richard Elliot
events.note: Tenor saxophonist out of Tower of Power, now a fixture of the contemporary-jazz circuit. Know what you are buying: this is the polished end of the form, played very well.

events.title: House Party
events.note: A recurring club night at the Ritz with no DJs named on the listing. Included because South Bay club programming is thin enough to be worth knowing about, not because the booking is known.

events.title: Usher, Chris Brown, Mario, Eric Bellinger
events.note: A stadium package, playing Friday and Saturday. Listed for completeness — findable without any help from this digest, and the brief deprioritises stadiums for exactly that reason.

events.title: The Tale of the Princess Kaguya
events.note: Isao Takahata's last film, drawn in charcoal and watercolour that appears to be dissolving as you watch. Part of Some Nostalgic Place, BAMPFA's Takahata retrospective.

events.title: Elevator to the Gallows
events.note: Louis Malle's debut, with the score Miles Davis improvised in one night watching the footage. From the French Noir series. If you only see one repertory screening this week, this is a strong candidate.

events.title: Visitacion Valley Night Market and Block Party
events.note: The neighbourhood's first-ever night market, run by All My Usos with the Samoan Community Development Center and Pasifika By Design — Pacific Islander food, music and street dancing on Leland. Free. The T Third is a short walk from Arleta or Sunnydale.

events.title: Union Square Dances
events.note: Live music and a beginners' lesson, then open dancing in the square — the style rotates weekly between tango, salsa, swing, country-western and Bollywood. No partner or experience needed, and nobody watching cares.

events.title: Friday Nights at OMCA
events.note: Block party in the garden — DJs, food trucks, half-price gallery admission and Mildred Howard's Poetics of Memory in the Great Hall. BART Lake Merritt is two minutes; downtown Oakland garages shut their gates at seven on weekdays.

events.title: Music on the Square: Starman SF
events.note: A Bowie tribute act closing out the twentieth season of free Friday concerts on the square. A tribute band, so never the headline recommendation — but it is free, it is outdoors, and the square fills with families by half past five.

events.title: San Francisco Critical Mass
events.note: The last-Friday mass ride that started here in 1992 and spread to sixty countries. Gathers at Justin Herman Plaza, leaves around six. If you are driving downtown on Friday evening, this is your street-closure warning.

events.title: San Jose Giants and post-game fireworks
events.note: Friday fireworks with a musical theme, and the display is visible free from the streets around the park if you do not want the game. Parking at Excite is genuinely hard; VTA Race St is an eight-minute walk.

events.title: Pokémon XP: Fan Fest and World Championships
events.note: The world finals, running Friday to Sunday, with a free public activity zone alongside the badged competition. Listed for the free half — the brief excludes conferences except where there is open public programming, and here there is.

events.title: Shotz: Maxxing — seven world-premiere short plays
events.note: Seven brand-new short plays written to a monthly theme and staged the same month. Five dollars. The failure rate is part of the format and so is the occasional very good one.

events.title: The Big Gay Sleepover
events.note: Drag and dancing at the city's central queer cabaret, pitched as a slumber party. Fifteen dollars, and the room is small enough that the performers are two feet away.

events.title: The Roots, Nas, De La Soul
events.note: Three foundational acts on one bill, with the best live band in hip-hop backing the night. Illmatic and 3 Feet High and Rising in the same evening, twenty minutes from the origin. The event of the week, and it is the closest thing on the list.

events.title: Brad Mehldau: Ride Into the Sun
events.note: Mehldau's Elliott Smith project, reworking those songs through his own harmonic language — closer to Schumann than to a covers set. SFJAZZ presents, which is how there is any world-class jazz in the Bay this week at all with Miner Auditorium dark. An art-deco palace is the right room for it.

events.title: Tori Amos, Bartees Strange
events.note: Thirty years on from Little Earthquakes and still playing the Bösendorfer like an argument. Bartees Strange is a genuinely interesting support choice rather than a filler. Second Greek show of the week; layers again.

events.title: J. Cole
events.note: Two nights at the arena, Saturday and Sunday. An arena booking, so listed rather than featured — and it conflicts directly with the far better hip-hop bill at Shoreline on the Saturday.

events.title: Vanilla Ice, Rob Base, Young MC, C+C Music Factory
events.note: A late-eighties package tour on a hillside. Rob Base's It Takes Two remains an genuinely great record; the rest is what it is. If you want hip-hop this Saturday, Shoreline is the serious answer.

events.title: El Tri
events.note: Alex Lora's band have been the spine of Mexican rock since 1968 — blues-based, unreconstructed, and still filling halls. Two nights, Saturday and Sunday. A legacy act in the fullest sense.

events.title: Sonu Nigam
events.note: One of the most recorded playback singers in Hindi cinema, and a reliable arena draw in the South Bay. Deprioritised as an arena show, but worth knowing it is on.

events.title: Simon Phillips & Protocol 6
events.note: The drummer from Toto and a hundred other sessions, leading his own instrumental fusion band. Two nights, Saturday and Sunday. Technical to a fault, which is either the appeal or the objection.

events.title: Bill Kirchen with Nina Gerber
events.note: The Telecaster on Hot Rod Lincoln, and the man who more or less invented dieselbilly. Nina Gerber is one of the finest accompanists in West Coast folk. A very good night in a seated room.

events.title: Arnocorps, FleXx Bronco, The Memphis Murder Men
events.note: An action-adventure hardcore band whose entire repertoire is Schwarzenegger films performed in character and full costume. Absurd, committed, extremely loud. 21+.

events.title: Mini Trees
events.note: Lexi Vega's project — quiet, precise indie-pop written from the drum kit outward, which gives it an unusual rhythmic spine for the genre.

events.title: In Shame, Dread Spire, Marrower, Rotterdam
events.note: Four heavy bands in a small room on a Saturday. This is the kind of bill Gilman and the Stork Club keep alive in the East Bay when nobody else will book it.

events.title: Secret Psychedelica: Virgo World
events.note: A long night of psychedelic electronic music with the lineup withheld until close to the door, which is the party's whole conceit.

events.title: Spirited Away, 25th anniversary
events.note: Miyazaki's bathhouse, projected in a 1,400-seat picture palace with a Wurlitzer. The right way to see it, and a rare matinee that is worth planning a Saturday around.

events.title: Rocketman Sing-Along
events.note: Lyrics on screen and an audience that does not need them. The Castro's sing-alongs are a genuine local institution rather than a gimmick. Doors 7.

events.title: Tongues Untied
events.note: Marlon Riggs's 1989 essay film on Black gay identity — poetry, documentary and confrontation at once, and still the thing that got the NEA defunded. Part of Made in Berkeley: The House That Zaentz Built.

events.title: Arboretum Cycle — Nathaniel Dorsky & Jerome Hiler
events.note: Silent 16mm from the two San Francisco filmmakers who have spent fifty years making light and foliage into a devotional practice. There is no way to see this outside a screening like this one.

events.title: Goodbye, Dragon Inn
events.venue: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts
events.note: Tsai Ming-liang's near-wordless elegy for a dying cinema, shown in a screening room. Fifteen dollars covers the film, snacks and the galleries — the best-value ticket of the weekend.

events.title: Stanley Kwan's Center Stage, 4K restoration
events.note: Maggie Cheung as the 1930s Shanghai film star Ruan Lingyu, in a biopic that keeps stopping to interrogate its own project. One of the great performances, newly restored.

events.title: Ambrose Trataris: Daisy-Chain<><><>Star-Connection
events.note: An audiovisual performance at Gray Area's Grand Theater, which is the only room in the city reliably programming this kind of work. Neither time nor price was posted; details are thin.

events.title: Castro Carnival Block Party
events.note: A free block party of LGBTQ+ artists, live music and drag on a closed block of Noe. Family-friendly and daylight-hours, which distinguishes it from most of what the Castro throws. Muni Castro is a minute away and driving is pointless.

events.title: 17th Annual Spirit & Soul Festival
events.note: Six blocks of Macdonald Avenue closed for live performance, a classic car show, artisan stalls and a youth zone. Seventeen years old and free. Richmond is not named in the brief's region lists — filed east-bay by proximity.

events.title: Union Square Free Outdoor Movie Night
events.note: A film projected in the plaza after dark, free and unticketed. Downtown fog rolls in early even in August — this is a blanket event, not a T-shirt one.

events.title: Crab Cove Fish Festival
events.note: East Bay Regional Parks doing what it does well — touch tanks, naturalists and the bay shore, free all day. Genuinely good with children and not bad without them.

events.title: Bon Marché 2nd Hand Market
events.note: Vintage and secondhand sellers in and around a Solano Avenue gallery. Small, curated, and over by four.

events.title: Richmond Art Center 90th Birthday Party
events.note: Ninety years of one of the oldest community art centres in California, marked with open galleries and free admission. Three hours' walk from the Spirit & Soul Festival on the same afternoon — do both.

events.title: Poetry in the Parks
events.note: Guided writing on the shoreline with the bridge in view, run free by the Parks Conservancy. Registration required. Also runs Sunday on landscape poetry.

events.title: Scumdance Film Festival
events.note: Nine hours of underground and no-budget film in a fifty-seat storefront theatre. Eighteen dollars for the day. The name is the mission statement.

events.title: Mission Missives Zine Expo
events.note: A zine fair at the youth arts organisation's Mission space, free and open. Could not be verified against Youth Art Exchange's own calendar — confirm before making the trip.

events.title: Pub in the Park: giant inflatables and summer picnic
events.note: The city's end-of-summer park party — inflatables, beer garden and food, free to enter. Redwood City's third free public event of the week, which is more than the whole Peninsula usually manages.

events.title: Free Museum Day: de Young and Legion of Honor
events.note: Both Fine Arts Museums free to Bay Area residents with ID for the day. The single highest-value free thing on the calendar this week, and it applies at Lincoln Park as well as Golden Gate Park.

events.title: BATS Improv opens its 2026 run
events.note: The long-running improv company beginning a run at Fort Mason that carries through to December. Neither time nor price was listed on the centre's calendar.

events.title: Black Music Festival: Miss Faye Carol, Tuck & Patti, Paula West, Rico Pabon, Professor Kee, Ian Kelly, Tia Nomore
events.note: Seven acts spanning four generations of Bay Area Black music — Faye Carol has been the Dean of it for fifty years, Paula West is the finest jazz singer in the city, and Tia Nomore comes from a completely different Oakland. Fifty dollars for all of it, in the gilded balcony room. The bill of the week.

events.title: Diana Ross
events.note: Diana Ross on a Saratoga hillside in front of 2,500 people. Whatever the voice does or does not still do, the room is a tenth the size of where she would normally play, and that is the entire argument. Hillside shuttle from the $20 lot; it is cold up there after dark.

events.title: BonPOP 2026: 5th Anniversary Bon Odori Festival
events.note: Taiko, Bon Odori dancing, memorial lanterns, yukata dressing and a vendor fair — a reimagined ancestral festival opened to anyone, whatever their faith. Free to SF residents with ID and to under-4s, veterans and Gardens members; $17 at the gate otherwise. State the mechanism, because it catches people out.

events.title: Cyberdelia: Hackers Screening and Cyberpunk Dance Party
events.note: The club is redressed as the nightclub from the 1995 film, the film is screened, and then everyone dances to electro and big beat in costume. Exactly the sort of thing DNA Lounge exists for. 18+.

events.title: Chinatown Free Sunday Family Block Party
events.note: Grant Avenue closed to traffic for the morning — performances, games and food on the neighbourhood's main street. Free. Muni 30 or 45 stops two minutes away; parking in Chinatown is a $10-an-hour garage and a wasted half-hour.

events.title: Golden Gate Park Band: Symphony in the Park
events.note: A free municipal band playing the Music Concourse bandshell every Sunday since 1882 — the 144th season. Bring something to sit on; the benches go early and the concourse is stone.

events.title: Golden Gate Park Sunday Roller Disco
events.note: Forty years of a sound system on a patch of asphalt off JFK and people in skates. Free, no skill floor, and one of the genuinely unrepeatable things about this city.

events.title: Lindy in the Park
events.note: Free swing dancing on the closed drive every Sunday since 1997, with a beginners' lesson at the start. Three park events run within a few hundred metres of each other this Sunday — this, the band, and the roller disco.

events.title: Brazilian Day White Party and Lavagem Festival
events.note: A lavagem — the Bahian ritual washing of the church steps — restaged on Shattuck, with samba and capoeira after. Free, donations encouraged. Wear white; that part is not optional in spirit.

events.title: Cape & Cowl Comic Con
events.note: 150-plus artists in a brewery on the old naval air station, with the city skyline across the estuary behind them. Free to get in, artist-run, and a great deal more pleasant than a convention hall.

events.title: Free Oakland Up Market
events.note: A free community market — everything given away rather than sold. The listing gives no street address, so confirm the location before setting out.

events.title: Tom Kenny & the Hi Seas, Michael Michael Motorcycle, Cape Fury
events.note: Yes, that Tom Kenny — the voice of SpongeBob fronting a surf-rock band, which he has done seriously for years. Silly premise, competent band, all ages.

events.title: DITZ, Strange Cities, Rabbit
events.note: Brighton noise-rock — abrasive, tightly wound, and considerably heavier live than the records let on. A strong Sunday booking.

events.title: Kasbo
events.note: Swedish producer working the melodic, wistful end of festival electronic music. Big-room sound, small-hours emotions.

events.title: Wicked Messengers
events.note: A 150-capacity Solano Avenue bar with a real booker. The name suggests a Dylan connection but nothing was verifiable — descriptor is a guess from the room's usual programming.

events.title: Josh Johnson
events.note: The Daily Show writer and stand-up whose specials he released free on YouTube, filling a 3,300-seat hall off the back of it. Not a chain comedy club — a genuine theatre booking.

events.title: Raiders of the Lost Ark, 45th anniversary in 4K
events.note: Shot in Marin, more or less. Forty-five years on and the boulder still works better with 1,400 people reacting at once. Doors 1.

events.title: Rear Window, 4K restoration
events.note: Hitchcock's single-set masterpiece, restored. A double bill with Raiders earlier the same day makes for a very good and slightly absurd Sunday at the Castro.

events.title: Eyes Wide Shut
events.note: Kubrick's last film, from the complete retrospective BAMPFA is running all autumn. It conflicts exactly with Rear Window at the Castro; both are worth it and you cannot do both.

events.title: Thick & Tired drag show
events.note: Free early-evening drag in a Divisadero art bar, $10 suggested for the performers — which you should pay. Done by eight, so it works as a warm-up rather than a whole night.
